terms.term: The difference between accrual versus cash accounting comes down to timing of work earned, expenses incurred, and payments. With the cash basis, you account only for the money you receive and spend in a given period. With accrual accounting, you account for what revenue you’ve earned and expenses incurred, regardless of whether the payments for these are made before or after the period.
Hours and cost related to labor and non labor for a current or multiple periods.
A budgeting approach that starts with individual departments or programs estimating their needs and then rolling them up into a final budget.
A financial plan that outlines the expected revenue and expenses for an IT department over a specific period.
Key metric used in financial planning which determines how much of the budget can be used for development (cash) versus capital expenditures.
Change the Business projects, which are included in our EC portfolio typically are adding significant functionality or enhancements. These types of projects normally have a start and end date.
Projects and activities that are typically a part of our discretionary budget.
The current expectation of the total costs of a project for the current fiscal year (synonymous with current forecast).
The expected cost required to complete the remaining work of a project.
An expense that is typically budgeted for NonEC/KTLO and therefore does not change over the budget year.
A contract written with detailed or high level deliverables or milestones stated over a period of time.
YTD actuals through the most recent complete month plus estimate to complete. We capture 11 forecasts during a fiscal year.
Document providing preliminary funding estimates for each portfolio or program serving as a starting point for setting high-level targets for the next fiscal year.
Initial budgetary goals set for a fiscal year/Estimates of the overall funding that will be available for different categories of IT spending.
Department managing the overall budget for IT and its projects.
Non-discretionary spending includes essential costs like maintenance contracts and annualized growth while discretionary spending allows for investments in new projects and initiatives.
Non-Discretionary Budget
A financial statement showing revenue against expenses for a division or company.
A group of related projects or programs that are managed together.
The process of selecting and organizing projects based on their strategic importance, business value, and alignment with the overall IT strategy.
A group of projects that are related to a specific objective or initiative.
A temporary endeavor undertaken to create a unique product, service, or result.
Why to do it, rules that apply (like for like cost type), level of detail required, & why.
Project demand represents the total funding required requested for all projects, while supply refers to the available resources (internal labor, external labor, equipment, etc.).
The selection, prioritization, and control of an organization’s projects and programs in line with its strategic objectives and capacity to deliver.
Savings or profit earned on investment (Project) over the cost of the investment (Project).
Run the Business and Keep the Lights On activities that exist to maintain existing systems.
Software Quality Management
Contracts specify the scope of a project but are open-ended. These contracts typically have resources or roles assigned with a corresponding rate.
A budgeting approach that starts with setting an overall budget target and then allocating resources to different departments or programs.
The budget is initially established based on projected revenue growth (top-down) and then broken down into subcategories and individual projects (bottom-up).
An expense that is typically budgeted for EC/Discretionary projects and due to its high impact and scrutiny can change over the budget year.
